notes:
WORKING TITLE: Eleven Springs

REGISTER DECISION, made from measurement before the design was written (manual step 1).

The archive cannot supply a prison-and-courtroom film. Cross-episode burn rates measured 2026-08-03: courtroom 23/24, letter 22/24, cell 20/24, prison 18/24, interrogation 18/24, handcuffs 7/7. The manual's cut-off is 20%. After 60 episodes the legal-genre shelf is spent.

The same measurement found the alternative register wide open: river 1/24, spring 2/24, bus 2/24, porch 3/24, snow 4/24, mirror 5/24, church 8/24, fence 8/24. Avoid clock 16/24, highway 19/24, playground 24/24.

YouTube demand measured the same day points the same way. 'Innocent man released after decades' medians 862,140 views across 8 channels; 'man exonerated after decades in prison' 537,216 across 6. The doctrinal framings collapse: 'forensic expert wrong testimony' medians 19,465 with 10 long-form videos already there, and 'prosecutor hid evidence' medians 1,068. The audience does not want the mechanism. It wants the years.

So: this film is about eleven springs that happened without her. The legal machinery — the bite mark, the informant, the DA's direction to re-examine timing — is carried by figure beats (quotes, timelines, numbers) over footage of the world outside continuing. Courtroom and prison imagery is permitted only as brief punctuation, never as the register.

SOURCE OF FACTS: Weimer v. County of Fayette, 972 F.3d 177 (3d Cir. 2020), read directly via CourtListener cluster 4778177; extract at episodes/_planning/measurements/WEIMER_FACTS.md. Every factual beat must trace to that opinion or to another primary source read by the writer, and go into a facts ledger before it enters a script.

LEGAL REVIEW: living people are named in the opinion, including a former District Attorney against whom allegations were pleaded but not proven. Treat as R3 — owner legal review required before publication, same handling as EP15 Theranos.
